utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, I move now to a decision. I now move to a decision by the Chamber, that is, to continue to hear the case today, although Judge Fluegge is for urgent personal reasons unable to hear the case. It will be of short duration as far as we can see now, and therefore Judge Moloto and myself have decided that it is in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case today. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I address a few matters. The first relates to the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin. On the 11th of December, P7010 was marked for identification during the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin. In relation to this document, on the 13th of February, 2015, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber to advise that it had uploaded into e-court document bearing 65 ter number 31772a, which are two pages of Kupresanin's testimony from the Karadzic case, and requested that, subject to the agreement of the Defence, these pages be admitted into evidence as Exhibit P7010. On the same day, the Chamber e-mailed the Defence to see if it had any objections to 65 ter 31772a being admitted. As of today's date, the Defence has not responded, and the Defence is hereby instructed to respond in court before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. MacDonald will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, yesterday we spoke about the 13th of July and your journey on that day, that you left Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje with Borovcanin, Pirocanac, you stopped at Sandici meadow around or just about 4.00 in the afternoon. You went further towards Konjevic Polje, turning around about Pervani and you then headed back towards Bratunac. On your way back, we had the radio call of Borovcanin telling someone to close the road to the traffic, and as I said yesterday the Chamber has heard evidence that someone was Oficir, and that Milenko Pepic was taken by Oficir to a bridge at Kravica village and told to wait for an order to stop the traffic. And finally we came to you, Borovcanin, and Pirocanac being back together at Sandici meadow, and that's where we paused yesterday. And what I'd like to do is to rejoin that journey where we left off. I'm going to ask that some more footage be played to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Before I do, just for the record and Your Honours' benefit, this is the footage we have from the BBC identical to the Pirocanac footage. I'm going to ask that it be played from 00.23.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Before we play it, let me just advise you this has been identified as just behind the largely destroyed house on Sandici meadow and that we're going to see some Bosnian Muslim men surrendering. You'll hear some dialogue, but I'm interested in the sound you hear behind the dialogue, particularly around the time we see the younger male take off his T-shirt. If I can now ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, you again said you would play the BBC version. That is the version which is not in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It is in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Both the original from Pirocanac and from the BBC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just I -- I missed that point. And then further you referred to Pervani. Yesterday we left off, just wondering -- it didn't ring a bell to me, Pervani, but it may well be that I missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours, I was at point 9, on the map. It's the area where we saw the Praga and the BOV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I now ask that that clip be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can pause here, please. Your Honours, I don't think the audio came on until about halfway through that clip. I wonder then if we could replay it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think it was not loud enough, then you can play it again. I -- of course I didn't hear the original, but I did hear the background sound which you were specifically drawing our attention to. And if you have any concerns, then of course the volume for the witness could be increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's not that, Your Honour. In my hearing, there was no audio for the first half of the clip, and I've had that before with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Play it again as good as you can technically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We've paused at 00.23.32.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the automatic fire and the explosion in the background there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the automatic fire, but not the explosion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if I may ask for the assistance of Madam Usher at this point and just play it one more time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And before I ask that it be played, Mr. Witness, the explosion happens just after the man begins taking his T-shirt off, if I can ask you to listen very carefully to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can play it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We've again paused at 00.23.33.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I think the automatic gun-fire was more clear there. Just before the second burst, there was an explosion. Did you hear it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard a blunt sound, the sound of a blunt object. I could hear the automatic fire very well, but the rest ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The Prosecution case, Mr. Jovicic, is that that sound you heard is a hand-grenade and that that hand-grenade and the automatic fire you hear is the start of the massacre at Kravica warehouse. Now, do you have any comment upon that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say whether that was a hand-grenade or some other explosive device. And as for the automatic fire, you can hear that, but I don't know where, what direction it is coming from. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: One final question before we move on to the next piece of footage. The Bosnian Serbs we saw in that clip, they did not react to that fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can move on to the next piece of footage. Again, you'll hear dialogue here. It's a man coming down to surrender and being directed across the road. But, again, I'd ask you to listen out for a sound in the background. That's at approximately 00.24.09.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd ask that we play from 00.23.50 to 00.24.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, did you hear what sounded like a car pulling away very quickly?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When Pirocanac is filming that footage, when he is at the largely destroyed house on Sandici meadow, are you by your car at that point?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if we have a car pulling away quickly, screeching away like that, you remember that happening on that day?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was a road. A lot of vehicles passed by, buses, lorries from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. Who was it who passed at that very moment I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just to be clear, I'm not talking about vehicles passing by or buses or lorries; I'm talking about a car being there and pulling away very suddenly, whether you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can clearly hear that in the footage, but I can't remember that moment. It is really possible that that happened, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution theory, Mr. Jovicic, the Prosecution position is that after the executions had begun at Kravica warehouse, some -- somebody heard that something had gone wrong, and this car is being sent to investigate that. Do you have any comment upon that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the incident in Kravica happened somewhat later. When we came by -- I don't know when this footage was made. I think it -- this happened after the incident at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like to move to one last piece of footage from this video. It's from 00.24.15 to 00.24.24. Before we play it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the second part of footage to which I would draw the attention of this witness to the audio that this had been alerted. The clip may catch some mumbling in the car at the start, but the part I'm interested in is the radio call that we hear clearly, one short line. I'd now ask that that be played. I'm obliged to Ms. Stewart. For the benefit of the booths, the transcript is page 15 in English and page 17 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Laser 2 is calling you."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We heard the line "Laser 2 is calling you." Laser 2 was the call-sign of Borovcanin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And just for the record, that piece of clip finished -- or paused at 00.24.24:4. Mr. Jovicic, by this point by that piece of footage, you had not yet received the panicky radio call from Miso Stupar to tell you something had gone wrong at Kravica warehouse, had you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, this video goes on and the last piece of footage we have on the 13th at Sandici meadow ends at 00.24.35, a short time later. Now, I'd suggest to you that it's shortly after the scene we've just seen that you leave and then you get the call that something has gone wrong at Kravica warehouse. So shortly after what we've just seen, you do get that call from Miso Stupar?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the encounter with General Mladic in the meadow in Sandici, we headed for Konjevic Polje. On the way to Konjevic Polje, Miso Stupar called us and he was in panic when he told us that something bad had happened at the Kravica farm. We turned around and went in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When you got that call from Miso Stupar, you went straight to Kravica warehouse; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on the road, the Sandici-Konjevic Polje road, and on that road we received that call. Once we received it, I turned the car around and I headed off towards Bratunac. And on the way to Bratunac, there is this farm where the incident had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd just like to be very precise in this next question. After you got the call and you turned around, you did not stop anywhere until you got to the farm or Kravica warehouse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We rushed towards the farm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand this as rushing meaning not stopping either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't stop anywhere, until later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until you went to the -- you arrived at the farm, Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once we passed the farm, we stopped for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when you refer to "the farm," that's the place where -- that's Kravica warehouse, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The place where the incident had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jovicic, if we play the raw footage on, we get 24 seconds of a cardboard ration box being filmed, and it's the Prosecution case that that filming of the cardboard ration box tapes over filming that was taken -- or footage that was taken of Kravica warehouse. Now, we have the footage or some of the footage from Kravica warehouse from a separate source, and I'd now like -- I'd like to move to that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have P01147. For the benefit of Your Honours, this is the compilation tape made for this trial. I'd ask that it be played from 00.36.18, and if we can pause when we have the part where it fades away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "There are dead Muslim soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We've stopped that 00.36.25:9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of automatic fire there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It's coming from the area you were passing at the time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was in the car, and it was very far to guess where that had come from. As I sit here today I have the same problem, and then I was in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, we're going to see the same scene in slow motion now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So can we please play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And we've paused at 00.36.56:8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You saw the bodies lying in front of the warehouse there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing them at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Kravica warehouse is on the right of your car; that means at that point you're driving back towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were driving from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac and the farm was on our right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, the bodies we saw there, they're in front of the part of the warehouse closest to Konjevic Polje; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's the closest to Kravica because the warehouse is in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if we can pull -- we can have P01132 and it's page 95 I would be looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, this is an aerial image taken of Kravica warehouse. Now, the red box is around Kravica warehouse and the blue arrow is pointing in the direction of Bratunac. What I'm saying to you is that the bodies we saw are on the side of the warehouse closer to Konjevic Polje, that is, to the right of the photograph. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the co-operative. The bodies were outside. And this is located just as you enter Kravica from the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask this question just one more time. Perhaps I'm not being sufficiently precise. But we see the co-operative, the warehouse, inside the red box. We see a blue arrow pointing towards Bratunac. The bodies we saw on the video, the bodies piled up outside the warehouse, they are closest to the end of the warehouse that is nearest to Konjevic Polje, that is, to the right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When you saw that footage in slow motion, the man walking in front of the bus, he was making a thumbs-up sign; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you play it again because I didn't see that. I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can play the slow-motion part that begins at approximately 00.36.25 -- sorry, 27, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's P1147?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The man we saw walking closest to the bus, he was making a thumbs-up sign; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he raised his closed fist. I didn't see thumbs-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on. You say in your statement that you stopped for Borovcanin to speak with Miso Stupar. Who is all there when Borovcanin stops to speak to Stupar?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which position do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, you drive past the warehouse and you stop there and Borovcanin speaks with Miso Stupar; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, who's all there when Borovcanin is speaking to Miso Stupar?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was very short. We stopped by the co-operative before moving on. An injured policeman of ours was being evacuated. Miso said briefly what he had to say. They got into the vehicle. They took with them the officer who had been injured, and we moved on towards Bratunac. It all happened in a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, the injured officer, that's Rade Cuturic whose nickname is Oficir; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: He gets into another vehicle. That vehicle is a Golf car; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He got into some sort of a vehicle. I think it was a Volkswagen Golf. He didn't get into our vehicle, into the other one. They took him to the health centre in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: When you stopped there, did you or Borovcanin or anyone else go towards the Muslim bodies lying outside the warehouse that you'd seen and attempt to ascertain if they were alive or in need of medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were descending from Sandici towards the co-operative, we had no idea what was going on. As we were passing by the co-operative where the incident happened, at first, since I was driving, I didn't notice anything before Borovcanin said, "Oh my God, what is this?" And then I turned my head and saw the bodies. And after that we stopped, having passed the co-operative. Ljubisa spoke briefly with Miso about the incident, and in the meantime they put the injured officer into the vehicle. And then we moved on to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I asked you when you stopped there for this discussion if you or Borovcanin or anyone else went towards the Muslim bodies you'd seen lying outside the warehouse, and whether you tried to ascertain if they were alive or in need of medical assistance. Do I take it from the answer you've just given me, the answer to my question is "no"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped. Ljubisa was in the car. He exchanged a few words with Miso Stupar. He didn't get out of the vehicle. I didn't get out of the vehicle. We moved a few minutes later following them to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So no, you didn't do that?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not get out. We did not come close to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Something else I would like you to help me with. I said to you earlier the entire footage regarding this French cardboard ration box that we see on the raw footage, that lasts approximately 24 seconds. The Kravica warehouse footage we've seen that you've seen today lasts 2 to 3 seconds. Now, you were there in the car. You stopped and you're looking at this scene. What was on that approximately 21 seconds that was taped over? What did you see there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any other footage. I didn't even know this footage exists. I saw it a couple of months later --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I can stop you there. I'm not asking about what footage you saw. You were there at the time. You pulled over and you see the bodies in front of the warehouse. Now, there is 21 seconds of footage that has been taped over that we do not have. What else -- apart from what we've seen on the footage, what else did you see at Kravica warehouse when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, I told you what I had seen in the moment when Borovcanin and I were passing by, but when I was coming back from Bratunac because Borovcanin had sent me back to kind of find out what had happened. Is that what you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm not -- it's not what I want you to say that's important, Mr. Jovicic. When we see this footage, the footage cuts, as we hear, automatic fire, and then the camera goes blank. Now, you stop after this footage is taken. You see more people being executed at Kravica warehouse, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it then. Let me tell you. On the way back, when we went from Sandici towards Bratunac as we were passing by the co-operative, at one point I did not realise that had happened, I didn't notice anything. But then Borovcanin said, "Oh my God, what is this?" And then I turned my head to the right and saw a heap of corpses. And then when we stopped after the co-operative, he had a short exchange with Miso Stupar and we went on towards Bratunac. At that moment, I didn't even know that the man sitting in the back behind me, Pirocanac, was filming. Now, this footage that you played, I didn't even know that there is any footage at all. I saw that footage only a couple of months later on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sir, it is the Prosecution's case that this footage was deliberately taped over because it shows very dramatic incriminating scenes. Now, you were there when Borovcanin -- when you stop and Borovcanin is speaking to Miso Stupar, I'm asking you: What did you see happening in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know if somebody deleted that or not. Second, I've already told you twice what I had seen at that moment and I can repeat it at any moment. I gave you an account of what I had seen. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarification on one little point. Did I hear you correctly say that you said Pirocanac was in the car with you and you were not aware that he was filming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you got in the car, you didn't see him carrying a camera or some filming equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know how it was? Since he got there with us, all the time he was there he filmed whatever he liked. He had the camera always with him. I didn't pay attention. I didn't keep tabs what he was filming when. Now, obviously since we have this footage, he was filming at that moment, but at that time I was focused on my driving and I didn't realise he was filming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand you better. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, the footage we see shows a number of bodies outside the warehouse on one side, and we hear automatic gun-fire. The Prosecution believes that after the camera goes off, that gun-fire continues and we know people on the other side of the warehouse were executed after people on the first side were executed. When you were there, you heard more gun-fire and it was the people on the other side of the warehouse being executed; is that not the truth?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, gun-fire was heard. We could hear it on the footage. Now, where it came from, I can't even estimate because I was in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, when you came back from Bratunac health centre and you come towards Kravica warehouse, that's what you see, isn't it, people on the other side of the warehouse being executed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going to cover that in slightly more detail in a moment, but before I do, after the footage we have of Kravica warehouse, so after the first time you pass it, you accompany Cuturic back to Bratunac health centre; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If the Prosecution can please have P01477.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, what you're about to say is an excerpt from the Bratunac health log on 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd ask for the second page in both languages. If we can focus in on the second line. It's 1490 along the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: We see a date and time, 13 July 1995, 1740 hours, and then the name of the person Rade, son of Milan, Cuturic. So, Mr. Jovicic, you and those you were accompanying got to Bratunac health centre shortly before 1740; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn -- well, when you get to Bratunac health centre, Borovcanin instructs you to go back to Kravica warehouse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You've already told us that when you get back you see killings taking place on the other side of the warehouse. Now, when you got back, you saw two men shooting into that side of the warehouse; that's right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And when I say "the other side of the warehouse," I mean the other side from the side which had the bodies outside of it, just to be clear; that's right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, looking from the road, it's on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can just be as clear as possible. There was one side on the footage we see -- we saw bodies outside of that side of the warehouse. That's the side in the direction of Konjevic Polje. When you get back, after stopping at Bratunac health centre, you see people shooting into the other side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just if you would not mind. Did I hear you say, Mr. MacDonald, when you got back after stopping at Bratunac health centre, you see people shooting into the other side; is that what you said? Or shooting the other side? It's not entirely clear to me what your question was and therefore there's a risk of translation -- of interpretation problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slowly and clearly put to the witness what you had on your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if we are talking about -- sorry to interrupt you again. If we are talking about the other side, buildings usually have four sides. What we are talking about is still that wall, that side of the warehouse that faces the road, isn't it? But, either to the right of that wall or that face of the warehouse or to the left of it, not the back facing away from the road, but all facing the road. That's what we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that clear to you, Witness, as well, that we're only talking about that part of the warehouse which is visible from the road, facing the road. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please put your question again to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, if I can perhaps make it clearer by dividing Kravica warehouse into two halves. On the footage, we saw bodies outside of one half of the warehouse, and that is the half which is in the direction of Konjevic Polje. Now, when you get back, you see two men shooting into the other half, the half in the direction of Bratunac; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Judge remarked on this very well. Every building has four sides. The upper side of the warehouse is facing Konjevic Polje. On that side, there is nothing. On the side of the building facing the road, if we are looking from the road at the site of incident, the bodies were on the right. And on the upper side, there is nothing. That side faces Konjevic Polje. Because the building, as we see on the footage, is rectangular. On the upper side, there's nothing. If we are looking at the co-operative from the road, the corpses were lying to the right, outside the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As I understand the question, sir, this time now you are coming back from the medical centre and what Mr. MacDonald is asking you is: At that time, did you not see people -- two people shooting on the opposite side of the building, the side opposite to the one where you had seen the bodies? Am I right, Mr. MacDonald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following: Could we use the photograph and could we use the cursor to make clear what we are aiming at so that everyone sees exactly what we are talking about. Could we have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then could I have the assistance of the usher and then I'll take it up to the point where the witness has answered the questions. Okay. Could we zoom in. Okay. Could I give some indication and could the cursor be moved into the square. Okay. Now could it be moved to the right and little bit further -- no, not further down. Further to the right, further to the right, further to the right, further to the right, further to the right, further to the right, further to the right. Witness, do you see the cursor now? Stop it now. Do you see the cursor now on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we say is the right end of the warehouse, and it is just in front of that part of the warehouse, if I understood you well, where you saw the bodies. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look carefully, here there is a wall in the middle that divides the warehouse into the right half and the left half. If you move the cursor a bit, it's in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's all fine. But where the cursor is now, is that approximately where you saw the bodies, that is, the right half of the -- in front of the right half of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bodies were, as far as I can remember at a distance from that dividing wall in the middle towards the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the right half -- in front of the right half of the warehouse. Now could the cursor be moved to the left. Further, further, further, further, further. Now -- stop there. I think that Mr. MacDonald is asking you that after you had returned from the Bratunac health centre whether you saw persons shooting into the warehouse in that left part of that warehouse, that's approximately where the cursor is now? Did you see people shooting into the warehouse in that left half of the warehouse when you had returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I returned, I saw them shooting at people; but, again, in the right half of the building. There was no shooting on the left side. They were shooting again on the right-hand side. There was a door - and I believe you can see it here. Everything happened on the right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- Mr. MacDonald, you're cross-examining the witness. I just tried to go as far as what we heard as evidence and how I understood it in order to establish whether there was any confusion or not. I think for after the return I leave it to you further to further explore and further develop your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, when you went back and you saw these two men shooting, one would shoot and the other one would refill his gun; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And then when one finished his ammunition, the other one would replace him and continue shooting; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about these details. In any case, they were shooting in that direction. Now, how exactly they arranged it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: At the same time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please clarify where the witness said "in that direction," where, in the previous answers, there was no clear direction mentioned, what direction he referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, you said: "In any case, they," meaning the two men, "were shooting in that direction." What did you mean by "that direction"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the building, into the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And those men, they would give their empty magazines to others close to them and those others would refill their magazines; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm -- I think I may have one more question for the witness; however, I wonder if we could take the break just now and it may be that I have no more questions after the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take the break first. Mr. Jovicic, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I take my next item on the Kupresanin remaining issues list. It's about P6996, which was also marked for identification. P6996, an intercepted telephone conversation between Jovan Tintor and Mirko Jovic, marked for identification pending the formulation by the Defence of its objection, transcript pages 29692 to 94. The Chamber would like to hear if the Defence is in a position to formulate that objection. I don't know who's going to do it, and when, but it's a while ago now that the document was marked for identification so we would expect -- well, let's say, the objection to be formulated not any later than by Monday next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We understand, Your Honours. This is exactly what we are going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will hear from you. Perhaps where the witness has not arrived yet, another item in relation to the testimony of Goran Krcmar about P7171. This document was marked for identification pending an agreement between the parties as to which excerpts would be tendered, and the Chamber wonders whether the parties have come to an agreement and would appreciate if it would be informed about an agreement later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, you were considering whether or not you would put another question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm afraid it's multiplied into two questions. I hope that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I hope it doesn't go beyond that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, the Chamber has heard evidence in this case that hand-grenade handles were found outside and around the Kravica warehouse. Did you see at any point people throwing hand-grenades at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And today when we looked at the Kravica warehouse footage in slow motion, I asked if you saw the man walking beside the bus giving a thumbs-up, and you said to you that looked like a closed fist. What, in your opinion, does it signify when somebody raises a closed fist at a camera that is filming them?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen this man before and I never saw him gesticulating in that way before. I don't know what that means. I don't even know whether he realised that he was being filmed. Today was the first time I ever saw this footage featuring that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacDonald. Any further questions in re-examination, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovicic, just to orientate ourselves in time and space, could you tell us, to the best of your recollection and knowledge, what is the distance between the place that we referred to as Sandici meadow and the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Sandici pass to the Kravica warehouse, there is about 1500 metres or somewhat less. This is my estimate, or rather, a guesstimate, about 1500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, after General Mladic left Sandici, after he had addressed the prisoners, how long after that did you head in the direction of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a very short while. We lingered on just for a short while and then we headed for Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice anybody while you were there, did you notice any of the prisoners in the meadow being taken from there in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The next thing I would like to ask you is this: Could you give us an estimate of the distance between the Kravica warehouse and the Bratunac outpatient's clinic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, in general, the Chamber is better assisted by measurement on maps than by estimates, rough estimates - sometimes right, sometimes wrong - by witnesses. So why would you not agree with the Prosecution on what that distance is? Then we have a precise indication rather than a rough estimate by a witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the Prosecutor and me could agree on the distance. This was supposed to be my foundation. I will proceed with my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were in a car. How long did you take you [as interpreted] to travel that distance between Kravica and the outpatient clinic in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 20 to 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like us to look at P1477.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the central part, which is a protocol number 1491.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, does the name Krsto Dragicevic ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the special police of the MUP of Republika Srpska. I believe that he was in the Sekovici Detachment in the Skelani Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It says in this protocol that on the 13th of July, 1995, he was admitted at the outpatient's clinic. Do you know what had happened to this member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I heard, he was wounded in the same incident that had taken place at the farm, together with Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the name was of the member of your unit who was killed in the incident?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was Krsto. I can't remember. I know that he was seriously wounded and he succumbed to his wounds later. I know that one member of our unit did get killed in that incident, but I really can't remember who it was. Perhaps it was Krsto.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did there come a moment when you heard or saw the wounded person being brought into the outpatient clinic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as we arrived there, Borovcanin sent me back. So I was there for a very short time. Borovcanin got off the car, and I was about to get out of the car, he ordered me to go back to the farm to see what had happened. I went there and I learned that a member of our unit had been killed and that the officer, Rade, was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me finish with the following question: When did Rade Cuturic, also known as Oficir, get killed?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was in 1995, somewhere in the area of Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic, we have no further questions for you. Thank you on behalf of the General Mladic Defence.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO JOVICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. MacDonald, before I ask you whether you have any further questions to the witness -- was the last two, three minutes, was there anything which is in dispute between the parties, that is, about Mr. Dragicevic who may have died, whether it was about -- whether Mr. Cuturic later died. I don't know how that appears from cross-examination, but is there -- was there any matter of dispute so that we would be aware of that? And I'm talking about since we looked at this record of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, just because of my history with this, I don't believe that any -- I'm not aware of a dispute why certain things would be emphasised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not exactly sure, though the death of someone, so that you know he's not being called as a witness might have been helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although -- Mr. -- it doesn't arise from cross-examination why Mr. Cuturic was not called as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, and I don't think so. I was just saying that that -- you might find that helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, you'll understand why I asked this question because most of what was said, and apart from if you don't call a witness for any specific reason, then of course you could tell us. Just say, well, we can't call him because he died. So, therefore, could you please keep in mind that re-examination is to clarify matters which are in dispute and which arise from cross-examination. Any further questions, Mr. MacDonald?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Jovicic, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions that were put to you by the parties, questions that were put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again, and you may now follow the usher. And the usher is invited to escort the next witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd ask that myself and my colleague Mr. Corliss be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see we get, in return, we get Ms. Edgerton. Meanwhile I use the time again to deal with a matter related to the testimony of Goran Krcmar. It's about associated exhibits. Because in relation to the Witness Krcmar, there was 17 associated exhibits tendered pursuant to the Rule 92 ter motion; however, these associated exhibits were not tendered with the witness in court due, in part, to the fact that the translations - which were not CLSS translations - did not correspond to the B/C/S originals. The Chamber would like to know whether the Defence can, one, confirm whether or not it still intends to tender the 17 associated exhibits or whether it would formally withdraw some or even all of them; and, two, say when it expects to have CLSS translations for the associated exhibits that require translation. When do you think we could receive an answer, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by Monday, about the same time as we're supposed to provide you with the answer to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to address you with a procedural issue. I was asked by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this -- does the witness have to attend that? And is it of such urgency that we should let the witness wait now or could we do it at the end of this session, after we have the witness sent for a short break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness can be present. I don't see a problem in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but is it needed to do it when the witness is waiting for us or could we do it at the end of the session we're in now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no -- we can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait. We'll first proceed with the witness, who is standing there now ready for one or two minutes, and we'll hear from you at the end of this session, Mr. Stojanovic. Witness, may I take it that you're Mr. Micic. Mr. Micic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. May I? I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find Mr. Ivetic to your left, standing. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And perhaps with the assistance of the usher, I can pass a hard copy of his statement to opposing counsel before going to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. Can you please state your full name and last name for our record.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Good day. My name is Dusan Micic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at this time, Your Honours, I would call up in e-court 65 ter number 1D4472.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this statement from the Karadzic proceedings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could please turn to the last page of the same in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise whose signature we see here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: My own.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the date that is recorded here, is that in accord with your recollection of the date when you would have signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Subsequent to signing this statement, did you have occasion to read the same fully, to verify that everything is correctly recorded therein?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is everything accurately recorded therein?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if I were to ask you questions today based on the same facts and topics as in your written statement, would your answers today be the same as recorded in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, by and large, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, since you've taken a solemn declaration to tell the truth today, can we then conclude that the answers as contained in your written statement are truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 1D4472 into evidence. There are no associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D977, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, D977 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would now read the witness summary, a copy of which has been given to the booths. The witness, Dusan Micic, was born in Bratunac municipality. In early May 1992, he was mobilised and assigned to the military police in Bratunac, which was part of the Territorial Defence. Members of the military police who were lacking discipline or engaging in criminal acts were removed by the commander. Further processes against them were carried out by the civilian police because military courts were not yet in function. While patrolling the town, when passing the Vuk Karadzic school, he saw unfamiliar soldiers taking people out of the school. Later it turned out the majority of these soldiers were paramilitaries. He did not note any abuse at the school. In March 1993, the witness joined the civilian police as a reservist. In addition to work as a patrolman, he became part of the PJP from the Zvornik centre. He was commander of the 3rd Platoon of the 1st Company of the Zvornik PJP. The PJP wore camouflage military uniforms with the PJP insignia on the sleeves. On July 1995 as part of the PJP, he was in Potocari and saw General Ratko Mladic distributing cigarettes and food to Muslim civilians. He saw that many members of his unit also gave food and water to the Muslims gathered there. After the funeral of his slain PJP colleague, the witness was sent with other members of his PJP company to Baljkovica because a VRS unit had been surrounded by the enemy. Many Serb police and soldiers were casualties at this location; 80 were killed and over 100 wounded. The Muslims who were breaking through towards Tuzla were appearing from all sides. This lasted the entire day. And that concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to ask you some questions to clarify some portions of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could first turn to paragraph 3 on page 1 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, here you say that military policemen who were lacking in discipline and committing crimes were removed from service. How many such military policemen were there that this happened to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of perhaps two or three cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now I want to turn to paragraph 6 of the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, "perhaps two or three" is a rather vague answer. Could you tell us whether -- do you remember names of the two or three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't remember the name now. The commander was the kind of man who did not allow any unlawful behaviour. It was mostly about illegal entries into apartments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you say you are perhaps aware of two or three cases, which leaves it open that it could be one case or five cases or no case at all. Therefore, I'm -- do you remember two or three cases or are you uncertain about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember it, but I don't remember the names of the people involved. I'm quite sure about the cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember any other details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if we can focus at paragraph 6 of the statement, which is on the bottom of the page in both languages. You talk of the Vuk Karadzic school and seeing some unfamiliar soldiers taking people out of the school. Can you clarify for us what year this is taking place in?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, in this paragraph I was talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In your continued description of this incident, you say that: "It later turned out that the majority of these people in uniform were paramilitaries ..." What is the basis of your knowledge that they were paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, while going about my regular work and patrolling the town, I toured the town and I noticed men in camouflage uniforms with white belts and while belts across the chest but I didn't recognise any of them, which means that they were not from the Bratunac Brigade, they were not from Bratunac. After I don't know how much time, I learned from my colleagues and friends that these people had come from other areas, maybe Serbia, maybe Croatia, from another theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could look at paragraph 10 which is in the middle of the page, the incident when you and a colleague escorted two buses of Muslims to the Luke area, what year or time-period is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, it was 1992, probably in May, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at paragraph 12 which starts on the bottom of the page in Serbian and is at the bottom of the page in English, you mention a school. What school are you talking about in this paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: This school in the centre of Bratunac was then called Vuk Karadzic. Now it's called Branko Radicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the events that are described in paragraph 12, what time-period is involved, what year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Again, it's 1992, the month of May. Now I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we could look at paragraph 37, and this is on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you're moving to a different area, I would have two follow-up questions in order to better understand the testimony of the witness. First of all, you said you saw persons with white belts. What does that mean to you? What do white belts stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] White belts are a part of the uniform of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then another question I would have, you said they came from elsewhere. You learned from colleagues that they came from other areas, maybe Serbia, maybe Croatia. Was there no certainty about where they had come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, some were from Serbia, some were from Croatia. That's what people said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, finally in relation to paragraph 8 of your statement, you are saying in that paragraph that you were instructed by your commander during a working meeting that you should not go to that school. Did he give any explanation as why you shouldn't go there or what was the reason, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, somebody said at a meeting that he knew there was a large group of Muslims who had been placed in the gym of a school, and he didn't know what it was all about but he prohibited us from going near there because he didn't want us to have anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you were -- in your functioning, you were patrolling. And was any reason given why you should stay away from that -- from that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my personal opinion is that since the commander didn't know anything about it, that that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now forgive me, but if I have certain duties and if I don't know anything about a matter, I would rather go and see what happens so that you would know what happens. That is perhaps another kind of logic. Do you have any comment on why you say: Well, we don't know what happens there, so we stay out, rather than: We don't know what happens there; therefore, we go and explore it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what he said and the commander's word has to be obeyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. You never went there, you never saw personally a larger number of Muslims in the gym or in the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never went into the gym. I said a moment ago that while on patrol I passed by the school going along the high street, and I saw a group of people coming out. They were being taken to drink water. They acted normally. There was no ruckus, nobody was beating anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered my question. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a follow-up question. Sir, you said to the question -- in answer to the question by the Judge that white belts were part of the uniform of the military police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see in your statement you say now these were paramilitaries, not military police. On what basis did you come to the conclusion that they were paramilitaries and not military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At first sight, I thought they could be military police because of their white belts and cross-belts. And then later, from other people, I heard that it was a paramilitary unit. Even the paramilitary men could have worn white belts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could have, but did they? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, if you say they can, anybody can do anything; but whether a person has done something is a fact. Now, I want to know if you don't know whether they did wear on that day -- paramilitaries were wearing white belts, how do you come to the conclusion that these were paramilitaries? Civilians could also wear white belts. And the reason I'm asking this question is because you know that white belts are part of the uniform of the military police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know these men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I inferred that they were people from outside, not local people, that they were not from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my question. I don't know -- it doesn't matter where they came from, but your knowledge was that military police uniform has as part of it white belts. On what basis do you come to the conclusion that these are not military police but paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I heard that later from my colleagues, from my friends, that's what people said around Bratunac and that's the same as my own conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 6 in both languages and focus on paragraph 37 of your statement. And here you are discussing the situation at Baljkovica. For the record, can you describe for us where this location is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Baljkovica is approximately 20 kilometres away from Zvornik in the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you list here the casualties incurred by your forces. Did you have any idea or indication of the size of the opposing enemy forces that engaged you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, after the fighting was over, when I was returning from the mission, I heard in Zvornik that the Muslims outnumbered us perhaps 5:1 or even 10:1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what was the size of the combined police and army forces on the Serb side at that location engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, where I was there were about 300 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what kind of armaments or weapons did the enemy side use in this engagement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: In that skirmish, they used all kinds of weapons, starting with infantry weapons to artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What kind of artillery was involved?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I remember clearly that during that night after I arrived at Baljkovica with my unit, not far from my unit - I don't know how many kilometres away - they had captured three self-propelled artillery pieces from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And were those three self-propelled artillery pieces from the Serbian side used by the Muslim side during this engagement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: During that skirmish, they mostly used these self-propelled artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you indicate in your statement that you believe you stayed there one day and you're not sure about the night. Do you have any idea of how long the combat or skirmishing lasted in that area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Well, the fighting went on almost all day, from early morning hours to the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, on behalf of General Mladic and the rest of the team, I thank you for answering my questions today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Micic, could you be a bit more precise as when you arrived -- as you said you were sent by -- you went by bus to Baljkovica. When did you leave, when did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm more interested in the time of the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived in my unit the night before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Edgerton. You find Ms. Edgerton to your right, Mr. Micic. Ms. Edgerton is counsel for the Prosecution. Carefully listen to her questions and answer them. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I want to start very quickly by asking you just a couple of questions about your platoon that you commanded. Now, that was made up of about 20 people; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: There were more, around 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And those were people from Zvornik, Milici, Bratunac, and the Skelani police stations; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I was commander of the 3rd Platoon. There were not people from Zvornik, actually. I was commander of the 3rd Platoon, and I had under me members from Milici, Skelani, and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Okay. So when you said in your statement that - and it's in paragraph 32 - when you talked about going with policemen from your station in Bratunac to your colleague's funeral on the afternoon of the 13th, that means the majority of your platoon stayed in Sandici; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, I just asked you the question. So did they or didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So the policemen from Milici and Skelani, the PJP members of the 3rd Platoon of the 1st Company from Milici and Skelani remained in Sandici; do I understand you right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the witness's answer was not heard. He said "yes," he said "da."

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you confirm what I just put to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, what you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, my colleague Mr. Ivetic asked you a couple of questions about your deployment to Baljkovica, and I just want to help you along a little bit in terms of when this took place, and I'd like to do that by showing you a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 4082, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So this is a combat report created by Ljubisa Borovcanin for the period of July 10 to 20, 1995, and you know that Mr. Borovcanin was in command of MUP units in the Zvornik area during this period. And I'd like to take us to the entry for the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's at ET and B/C/S page 3, please. I'll just wait for a second until we see the English one. Great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, just have a look at the third -- give me a second. At the third paragraph under that heading, and it says: "In the afternoon," referring to the 15th of July, "an offensive MUP combat group comprising the 2nd and 4th Special Police Detachments and a tank and a Praga and a BOV 20/3, a mortar platoon, and the 1st Company of the Zvornik Special Police Unit was sent in the direction of Donja Baljkovica and Crni Vrh to block the area and prevent a breakthrough towards Zvornik by a strong enemy column ..." So when it talks about the 1st Company of the Zvornik Special Police Unit, that's your company; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So it's fair to say that your deployment to Baljkovica was on the afternoon of the -- started on the afternoon of the 15th of July, 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Most probably in the afternoon or early evening that we arrived at Baljkovica. As for Crni Vrh, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I have this as a Prosecution exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the part that has been presented to the witness has been read into the record and the witness has given his testimony about that. We've heard no other testimony linking other parts of this document to the witness's knowledge. It's a five-page document, at least in the translation, I don't know the original, so there's a lot of information in there that we know nothing about and whether this witness has any knowledge of the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm more than happy to keep coming back to this document during the course of the cross-examination, and probably at that point Mr. Ivetic might effectively change his mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't -- well, whether he changes his mind or not is still to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll tender it later, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll tender it -- should we mark it for identification at this moment, in view of what Ms. Edgerton announced would happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be MFI P7271, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7271 is marked for identification. If you are going to use it very often, Ms. Edgerton, the original has some handwritten English text on top of it, document number 5, four pages, which, by the way, is not -- well, I couldn't say translated into the English version but does not appear in the English version. And, of course, that is four pages, is easy to find out because that's what it is in the original. But document number 5 is a puzzling annotation. If you would spend any time on it, sooner or later, please do so, and also why it doesn't appear in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And now you spoke, Mr. Micic, about the artillery pieces that the Muslims were using and mentioned that those forces had captured three self-propelled artillery guns from the Serbian side. And those were, you can confirm this, just 76-millimetre artillery pieces, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I don't really know much about this kind of ordnance. All I know is that those were three self-propelled anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So since you know that they're anti-aircraft guns, what kind of calibre were they?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you. I'm not expert in these things. I don't know about the calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Fine. And since you were there at the time, you would know that those three guns were captured as a result of what the Zvornik -- the Drina Corps Command -- actually, let me rephrase that. Those three guns were recaptured as a result of what a VRS commander described as a synchronised kamikaze attack with numbers of the masses of people streaming towards your lines, jumping on them to take control. You know that, don't you, everybody was talking about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: What am I supposed to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're supposed to tell us whether you knew that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that the guns had been captured sometime before sunrise because my men who were deployed in that sector had stopped some people who were running for their lives away from the Muslims, and that's how I heard these guns had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. So let's go through this step by step. You -- on site, you knew that the Muslims had penetrated Serb lines; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You knew --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: That's why I was there in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you knew that Serb forces actually lost three trenches; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about three trenches. I knew about three self-propelled anti-anti-aircraft guns. And a gun is one thing and a trench is another thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You knew that your forces were suffering substantial casualties; you said that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You knew that even one of your own company was killed; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes, a man from my company, a man from Zvornik died there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You knew that the danger -- that the pressure and danger posed by these forces was putting your people at risk of being cut off and surrounded; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You knew that Serb forces couldn't hold out for long in the face of that kind of pressure, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if that kind of fighting continued, you would have taken just more losses; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So maybe then you would agree with me that to save the lives of the police, the soldiers, the Serb forces who were on those lines, the only logical military choice was to open up that corridor that got opened up later in the day on the 16th, to let the Muslim forces through; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN MICIC
utterances.text: I heard later that the corridor had been opened. I didn't know who made decisions, who had spoken to whom. I was not aware of those command decisions at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
